newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament adopts rail reform bill.
newsitem.headline: French parliament adopts rail reform bill.

text.p: The French parliament gave final approval on Friday to legislation aimed at sorting out the money troubles of the national railway SNCF by hiving off a large chunk of its debt into a new state company.

The legislation won final clearance in the national assembly by a vote of 38 to 22 after earlier receiving Senate approval. There are a total of 576 members in the national assembly but most were absent.

The measure involves spinning off 134.2 billion French francs ($24.08 billion) in debt out of a total 208 billion francs to a new state holding company which would in turn become owner of the rail infrastructure to be known as Reseau Ferre de France (RFF).

The measure has been strongly opposed by the two largest unions in the SNCF, the Communist-led CGT and the Socialist CFDT, which have said the reform amounts to a breakup of the railway and could open the way to privatisation of the network.

Transport Minister Bernard Pons, who has called the SNCF "the most indebted, most subsidised company in France", has said the reforms are necessary to put the railway on a sound financial footing. ($1=5.572 French Franc)
